\chapter{Boolean Analysis — Majority}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.Majority
\section{Overview}

This chapter records exact Fourier coefficients, relations between Fourier levels,
and dimensional monotonicity and asymptotics for majority on an odd number of variables.
Boolean inputs are expressed as signs, with false encoded by $1$ and true by $-1$;
majority returns the sign held by more than half of the coordinates, so no tie occurs.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Limiting majority level weights]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.majorityLimitWeight}
\leanok
For each $k\in\mathbb N$, define the real number
\[
 L_k=\begin{cases}
 \displaystyle\frac{4}{\pi k2^k}\binom{k-1}{(k-1)/2},& k\text{ odd},\\
 0,& k\text{ even}.
 \end{cases}
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Majority takes sign values]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.majority_isPmOne}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.isPmOne,BooleanAnalysis.majority}
\difficulty{4}
Let $m\in\mathbb N$, put $n=2m+1$, and define $M_m:\{\pm1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ by
$M_m(x)=1$ when more than $m$ coordinates equal $1$, and $M_m(x)=-1$ otherwise.
Then $M_m(x)\in\{1,-1\}$ for every $x\in\{\pm1\}^n$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Oddness of majority]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.majority_isOddFunc}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.isOddFunc,BooleanAnalysis.majority}
\difficulty{5}
Let $m\in\mathbb N$, put $n=2m+1$, and define $M_m:\{\pm1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ by
$M_m(x)=1$ when more than $m$ coordinates equal $1$, and $M_m(x)=-1$ otherwise.
Then $M_m(-x)=-M_m(x)$ for every $x\in\{\pm1\}^n$, where $-x$ negates every coordinate.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Nonnegative Fourier level weights]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.weightLevel_nonneg}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc,BooleanAnalysis.weightLevel}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n\in\mathbb N$ and $f:\{\pm1\}^n\to\mathbb R$; for
$S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ define
$\widehat f(S)=2^{-n}\sum_{x\in\{\pm1\}^n}f(x)\prod_{i\in S}x_i$, and for every
$k\in\mathbb N$ define $W_k(f)=\sum_{|S|=k}\widehat f(S)^2$.
Then $W_k(f)\ge0$ for every $k\in\mathbb N$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Vanishing levels above the dimension]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.weightLevel_eq_zero_of_lt}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc,BooleanAnalysis.weightLevel}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n\in\mathbb N$ and $f:\{\pm1\}^n\to\mathbb R$; for
$S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ define
$\widehat f(S)=2^{-n}\sum_{x\in\{\pm1\}^n}f(x)\prod_{i\in S}x_i$, and for every
$k\in\mathbb N$ define $W_k(f)=\sum_{|S|=k}\widehat f(S)^2$.
Then $W_k(f)=0$ for every $k\in\mathbb N$ with $n<k$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Fourier sums grouped by degree]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.sum_fourier_sq_eq_sum_weightLevel}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc,BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff,BooleanAnalysis.weightLevel}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n\in\mathbb N$ and $f:\{\pm1\}^n\to\mathbb R$; for
$S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ define
$\widehat f(S)=2^{-n}\sum_{x\in\{\pm1\}^n}f(x)\prod_{i\in S}x_i$, and for every
$k\in\mathbb N$ define $W_k(f)=\sum_{|S|=k}\widehat f(S)^2$.
For every $g:\mathbb N\to\mathbb R$,
\[
 \sum_{S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}}g(|S|)\widehat f(S)^2
 =\sum_{k=0}^n g(k)W_k(f).
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Stability generating function]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.noiseStability_eq_sum_weightLevel}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc,BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.noiseStability,BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.sum_fourier_sq_eq_sum_weightLevel,BooleanAnalysis.stability_formula,BooleanAnalysis.weightLevel}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n\in\mathbb N$, $\rho\in\mathbb R$, and $f:\{\pm1\}^n\to\mathbb R$; for
$S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ define $\chi_S(x)=\prod_{i\in S}x_i$,
$\widehat f(S)=2^{-n}\sum_{x\in\{\pm1\}^n}f(x)\chi_S(x)$,
$W_k(f)=\sum_{|S|=k}\widehat f(S)^2$ for $k\in\mathbb N$, and
$T_\rho f(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}}\rho^{|S|}\widehat f(S)\chi_S(x)$.
The noise stability $\operatorname{Stab}_\rho(f)=2^{-n}\sum_{x\in\{\pm1\}^n}f(x)T_\rho f(x)$ satisfies
\[
 \operatorname{Stab}_\rho(f)=\sum_{k=0}^n\rho^kW_k(f).
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Unit total Fourier weight]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.sum_weightLevel_eq_one}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc,BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.sum_fourier_sq_eq_sum_weightLevel,BooleanAnalysis.isPmOne,BooleanAnalysis.parseval_pm_one,BooleanAnalysis.weightLevel}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n\in\mathbb N$ and $f:\{\pm1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ satisfy $f(x)\in\{1,-1\}$ for every $x$;
for $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ define
$\widehat f(S)=2^{-n}\sum_{x\in\{\pm1\}^n}f(x)\prod_{i\in S}x_i$ and
$W_k(f)=\sum_{|S|=k}\widehat f(S)^2$ for $k\in\mathbb N$.
Then $\sum_{k=0}^n W_k(f)=1$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Prefix domination for geometric weights]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.sum_pow_mul_le_of_prefix_le}
\leanok
\difficulty{5}
Let $N\in\mathbb N$, $\rho\in[0,1]$, and $a,b:\mathbb N\to\mathbb R$ satisfy
$\sum_{k=0}^{j-1}b(k)\le\sum_{k=0}^{j-1}a(k)$ for every integer $0\le j\le N$ and
$\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}b(k)=\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}a(k)$, with sums over no indices interpreted as zero.
Then
\[
 \sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\rho^k b(k)\le\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\rho^k a(k).
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Vanishing even majority coefficients]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.majority_fourierCoeff_even}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.majority_isOddFunc,BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff,BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff_odd_even,BooleanAnalysis.majority}
\difficulty{1}
Let $m\in\mathbb N$, put $n=2m+1$, and define $M_m:\{\pm1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ by
$M_m(x)=1$ when more than $m$ coordinates equal $1$, and $M_m(x)=-1$ otherwise.
For $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ define
$\widehat M_m(S)=2^{-n}\sum_{x\in\{\pm1\}^n}M_m(x)\prod_{i\in S}x_i$.
If $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ has even cardinality, then $\widehat M_m(S)=0$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Exact odd majority coefficients]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.majority_fourierCoeff_odd}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff,BooleanAnalysis.majority}
Let $m\in\mathbb N$, put $n=2m+1$, and define $M_m:\{\pm1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ by
$M_m(x)=1$ when more than $m$ coordinates equal $1$, and $M_m(x)=-1$ otherwise.
For $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ define
$\widehat M_m(S)=2^{-n}\sum_{x\in\{\pm1\}^n}M_m(x)\prod_{i\in S}x_i$.
If $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ has cardinality $2r+1$ for an integer $r\ge0$, then
\[
 \widehat M_m(S)=(-1)^r\frac{\binom mr}{\binom{2m}{2r}}
                  \frac{\binom{2m}{m}}{2^{2m}}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Symmetry of binomial ratios]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.choose_div_choose_symm}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
For all $m,p,q\in\mathbb N$ with $p+q=m$, the binomial coefficients satisfy the real identity
\[
 \frac{\binom mq}{\binom{2m}{2q}}
 =\frac{\binom mp}{\binom{2m}{2p}}.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Duality of majority coefficients]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.majority_fourierCoeff_duality}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.choose_div_choose_symm,BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.majority_fourierCoeff_even,BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.majority_fourierCoeff_odd,BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff,BooleanAnalysis.majority}
\difficulty{5}
Let $m\in\mathbb N$, put $n=2m+1$, and define $M_m:\{\pm1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ by
$M_m(x)=1$ when more than $m$ coordinates equal $1$, and $M_m(x)=-1$ otherwise.
For $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ define
$\widehat M_m(S)=2^{-n}\sum_{x\in\{\pm1\}^n}M_m(x)\prod_{i\in S}x_i$.
If $S,T\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ satisfy $|S|+|T|=2m+2$, then
\[
 \widehat M_m(S)=(-1)^m\widehat M_m(T).
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Vanishing even majority weights]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.majority_weightLevel_even}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.majority_fourierCoeff_even,BooleanAnalysis.majority,BooleanAnalysis.weightLevel}
\difficulty{4}
Let $m\in\mathbb N$, put $n=2m+1$, and define $M_m:\{\pm1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ by
$M_m(x)=1$ when more than $m$ coordinates equal $1$, and $M_m(x)=-1$ otherwise.
For $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ define
$\widehat M_m(S)=2^{-n}\sum_{x\in\{\pm1\}^n}M_m(x)\prod_{i\in S}x_i$, and for every
$k\in\mathbb N$ define $W_k(M_m)=\sum_{|S|=k}\widehat M_m(S)^2$.
If $k\in\mathbb N$ is even, then $W_k(M_m)=0$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Exact odd majority level weights]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.majority_weightLevel_odd}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.majority_fourierCoeff_odd,BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff,BooleanAnalysis.majority,BooleanAnalysis.weightLevel}
\difficulty{5}
Let $m\in\mathbb N$, put $n=2m+1$, and define $M_m:\{\pm1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ by
$M_m(x)=1$ when more than $m$ coordinates equal $1$, and $M_m(x)=-1$ otherwise.
For $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ define
$\widehat M_m(S)=2^{-n}\sum_{x\in\{\pm1\}^n}M_m(x)\prod_{i\in S}x_i$, and for every
$k\in\mathbb N$ define $W_k(M_m)=\sum_{|S|=k}\widehat M_m(S)^2$.
For every odd $k\in\mathbb N$, put $r=(k-1)/2$; then
\[
 W_k(M_m)=\binom{2m+1}{k}
 \left(\frac{\binom mr}{\binom{2m}{k-1}}
            \frac{\binom{2m}{m}}{2^{2m}}\right)^2,
\]
where $\binom ab=0$ for $b>a$ and a real quotient with zero denominator is interpreted as zero.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Duality of majority level weights]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.majority_weight_duality}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.choose_div_choose_symm,BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.majority_weightLevel_even,BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.majority_weightLevel_odd,BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.weightLevel_eq_zero_of_lt,BooleanAnalysis.majority,BooleanAnalysis.weightLevel}
\difficulty{5}
Let $m\in\mathbb N$, put $n=2m+1$, and define $M_m:\{\pm1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ by
$M_m(x)=1$ when more than $m$ coordinates equal $1$, and $M_m(x)=-1$ otherwise.
For $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ define
$\widehat M_m(S)=2^{-n}\sum_{x\in\{\pm1\}^n}M_m(x)\prod_{i\in S}x_i$, and for every
$k\in\mathbb N$ define $W_k(M_m)=\sum_{|S|=k}\widehat M_m(S)^2$.
For every $k\in\mathbb N$ with $k\le2m+1$,
\[
 W_{2m+2-k}(M_m)=\frac{k}{2m+2-k}W_k(M_m).
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Two-step binomial recurrence]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.choose_add_two_mul}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
For all $N,k,a\in\mathbb N$ satisfying $N=k+a$, the binomial coefficients satisfy
\[
 \binom{N+2}{k}(a+2)(a+1)=\binom Nk(N+2)(N+1).
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Strict decrease of odd level weights]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.majority_weight_strictAnti}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.choose_add_two_mul,BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.majority_weightLevel_odd,BooleanAnalysis.majority,BooleanAnalysis.weightLevel}
\difficulty{6}
For each $q\in\mathbb N$, define $M_q:\{\pm1\}^{2q+1}\to\mathbb R$ to equal $1$ when
more than $q$ coordinates equal $1$, and $-1$ otherwise; for
$S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,2q+1\}$ define
$\widehat M_q(S)=2^{-(2q+1)}\sum_{x\in\{\pm1\}^{2q+1}}M_q(x)\prod_{i\in S}x_i$, and for
$k\in\mathbb N$ define $W_k(M_q)=\sum_{|S|=k}\widehat M_q(S)^2$.
For every $m,k\in\mathbb N$ with $k$ odd and $k\le2m+1$, one has
$W_k(M_{m+1})<W_k(M_m)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Limit and finite-dimensional error bound]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.majority_weight_tendsto}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.majorityLimitWeight,BooleanAnalysis.majority,BooleanAnalysis.weightLevel}
For each $q\in\mathbb N$, define $M_q:\{\pm1\}^{2q+1}\to\mathbb R$ to equal $1$ when
more than $q$ coordinates equal $1$, and $-1$ otherwise; for
$S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,2q+1\}$ define
$\widehat M_q(S)=2^{-(2q+1)}\sum_{x\in\{\pm1\}^{2q+1}}M_q(x)\prod_{i\in S}x_i$, and for
$k\in\mathbb N$ define $W_k(M_q)=\sum_{|S|=k}\widehat M_q(S)^2$.
For each fixed odd integer $k\ge1$, set
$L_k=\frac{4}{\pi k2^k}\binom{k-1}{(k-1)/2}$; then
$\lim_{m\to\infty}W_k(M_m)=L_k$, and for every $m\in\mathbb N$ satisfying
$k\le\lfloor(2m+1)/2\rfloor$ one has
\[
 L_k\le W_k(M_m)\le\left(1+\frac{2k}{2m+1}\right)L_k.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Decrease of cumulative majority weights]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.majority_prefix_weight_le}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.majority_isPmOne,BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.majority_weightLevel_even,BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.majority_weight_strictAnti,BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.sum_weightLevel_eq_one,BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.weightLevel_eq_zero_of_lt,BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.weightLevel_nonneg,BooleanAnalysis.majority,BooleanAnalysis.weightLevel}
\difficulty{5}
For each $q\in\mathbb N$, define $M_q:\{\pm1\}^{2q+1}\to\mathbb R$ to equal $1$ when
more than $q$ coordinates equal $1$, and $-1$ otherwise; for
$S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,2q+1\}$ define
$\widehat M_q(S)=2^{-(2q+1)}\sum_{x\in\{\pm1\}^{2q+1}}M_q(x)\prod_{i\in S}x_i$, and for
$k\in\mathbb N$ define $W_k(M_q)=\sum_{|S|=k}\widehat M_q(S)^2$.
For every $m,j\in\mathbb N$ satisfying $j\le2(m+1)+2$,
\[
 \sum_{k=0}^{j-1}W_k(M_{m+1})\le\sum_{k=0}^{j-1}W_k(M_m),
\]
where both sums are zero when $j=0$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Decrease of majority noise stability]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.majority_noiseStability_antitone}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.majority_isPmOne,BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.majority_prefix_weight_le,BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.noiseStability,BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.noiseStability_eq_sum_weightLevel,BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.sum_pow_mul_le_of_prefix_le,BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.sum_weightLevel_eq_one,BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.weightLevel_eq_zero_of_lt,BooleanAnalysis.majority,BooleanAnalysis.weightLevel}
\difficulty{5}
Let $m\in\mathbb N$ and $\rho\in[0,1]$, and for each $q\in\mathbb N$ define
$M_q:\{\pm1\}^{2q+1}\to\mathbb R$ to equal $1$ when more than $q$ coordinates equal $1$,
and $-1$ otherwise.
For any $d\in\mathbb N$ and $f:\{\pm1\}^d\to\mathbb R$, define
$\operatorname{Stab}_\rho(f)=\mathbb E[f(X)f(Y)]$, where $X$ is uniform on
$\{\pm1\}^d$ and, independently in each coordinate, $Y_i=-X_i$ with probability
$(1-\rho)/2$ and $Y_i=X_i$ otherwise; then
\[
 \operatorname{Stab}_\rho(M_{m+1})\le\operatorname{Stab}_\rho(M_m).
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Uniform majority spectral asymptotics]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.majority_weight_asymptotics}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.fourierWeightAbove,BooleanAnalysis.majority,BooleanAnalysis.weightLevel}
For each $m\in\mathbb N$, define $M_m:\{\pm1\}^{2m+1}\to\mathbb R$ to equal $1$ when
more than $m$ coordinates equal $1$, and $-1$ otherwise; for
$S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,2m+1\}$ define
$\widehat M_m(S)=2^{-(2m+1)}\sum_{x\in\{\pm1\}^{2m+1}}M_m(x)\prod_{i\in S}x_i$,
$W_k(M_m)=\sum_{|S|=k}\widehat M_m(S)^2$, and
$W_{>k}(M_m)=\sum_{|S|>k}\widehat M_m(S)^2$ for $k\in\mathbb N$, and put
$A=(2/\pi)^{3/2}$.
There exists one real constant $C\ge0$ such that for every $m,k\in\mathbb N$ with
$k$ odd, $k>0$, and $2k^2\le2m+1$, both estimates hold:
\[
 \left|\frac{W_k(M_m)}{A k^{-3/2}}-1\right|\le\frac Ck,
 \qquad
 \left|\frac{W_{>k}(M_m)}{A k^{-1/2}}-1\right|\le\frac Ck.
\]
\end{theorem}
